description: Employee EPF contribution rules used by the planner's EPF helper. These are EPFO payroll rules, not income-tax rules: they only suggest the Employee EPF figure, which stays an editable input. Dated so a mid-year change (such as a wage ceiling revision) is applied from the day it takes effect.

employee_rate_pct.note: Employee share, as a % of EPF wages (basic + DA). Some establishments are notified at 10% (fewer than 20 employees, certain industries); enter your payslip figure if yours differs.

employer_eps_pct.note: Pension (EPS) share of the employer's contribution, as a % of EPF wages up to the wage ceiling; the rest of the employer's share goes to EPF. Members who joined on or after 1 September 2014 earning above the then ceiling are not in EPS, so their employer share all goes to EPF. Whether EPS follows the revised 25,000 ceiling is not confirmed; the passbook is authoritative.

value.note: Statutory wage ceiling raised from 6,500 to 15,000 a month from 1 September 2014.

Raised to 25,000 a month by Gazette notification S.O. 5109(E) of 17 September 2026, effective that day. For September 2026, the old ceiling applies to days 1-16 and the new one to days 17-30. Some payrolls may apply it from October instead; your payslip is authoritative.

notes: EPF wages are taken as basic + DA as entered. Under the Labour Codes, allowances above half of total pay may also count as wages; if your payslip's EPF differs, enter it directly.
Contributions are rounded to the nearest rupee, as EPFO does.
In a month when the ceiling changes, the contribution is split by calendar days between the old and new ceilings.

sources.title: Employees' Provident Funds Scheme, 1952 and EPF & MP Act, 1952, s.6 (contribution rates)
Ministry of Labour & Employment notification G.S.R. 609(E), 22 August 2014 (wage ceiling 15,000)
Ministry of Labour & Employment Gazette notification S.O. 5109(E), 17 September 2026 (wage ceiling 25,000), as reported by caclubindia.com, keka.com and argus-p.com; official text not yet checked
